Why: Distinctive rhizomes, tall notched ligule and the golden seedhead. Some 2026 records were keyed from a "blue unknown with a tall ligule", which also fits big bluestem seedlings.
Could_be_confused_with: Big bluestem; timothy (both have a tall membranous ligule)

Why: Several records carry "or tall oat?" against unknown grasses; the big membranous ligule is shared with timothy.
2026 notes repeatedly read "could be IG or BB". Pre-seedhead the two are hard to separate.
Could_be_confused_with: Indiangrass; eastern gamagrass seedlings; sideoats grama

Why: Very large, distinctive. One of the few seeded grasses whose records can be taken at face value.

The recurring "blue mystery grass". Several 2026 records were assigned by matching to one uncertain determination at TE rather than keyed independently; one GF record was literally split 50/50 with meadow brome. A PV note reads "not sure if int wheat correct... Maybe quack".
Could_be_confused_with: QUACKGRASS (same tribe, both rhizomatous and glaucous - the single hardest pair in the mix); smooth brome; meadow brome; tall fescue

Why: Excluded taxon in the master name string, and one WB record reads "ANGIE MISID AS INT. WHEAT". Separation from smooth brome rests on auricles and leaf-margin hairs, which are lost in dried samples.
Also a common resident, so presence in a seeded plot is not evidence of establishment. Several records moved between smooth brome, quackgrass and tall fescue during review.
Recorded at only 6 farms. Notes include "Grama?" and, at WB, "prev said int. wheat". Without seedheads the hairy blade is the only cue.
Could_be_confused_with: Big bluestem; little bluestem; purple lovegrass; intermediate wheatgrass

Why: Essentially never found despite the second-highest seeding density in the mix (5.6 PLS/ft2). Either it failed everywhere or small plants were folded into other short grasses.
Could_be_confused_with: Hair grasses; small crabgrass; sideoats grama

Why: Pre-seedhead separation from broomsedge is unreliable and the notes say so ("Angie said probably broom but none in other plots"). One of the five seeded lots germinated at 12%, so a null result here is not a clean test.
Could_be_confused_with: BROOMSEDGE BLUESTEM (Andropogon virginicus, an abundant resident); purpletop

Why: Keyed as first-through-fourth guess in several notes ("Key'd = 1. slender wheat 2. smooth brome 3. intermediate wheat 4. timothy"). Absent entirely from 2026 despite 11 records in 2023-25, which suggests the earlier records were misassigned unknowns.
Could_be_confused_with: Smooth brome; intermediate wheatgrass; timothy; tall oatgrass

Why: One record in the whole project. Part of the "red bottom unknown" morphotype that was split across four wildrye codes.
Could_be_confused_with: Virginia wildrye; bottlebrush grass; Elymus sp.

Why: Same "red bottom unknown" cluster; notes ask outright "bigger leaves could be CA, smaller VA?".
Same cluster. One RV note reads "no other wild ryes in prev year... Safe bet, since sim and red collar" - an assignment by elimination, not by character.
Sits inside the fescue/ryegrass complex that drove the whole Schedonorus reclassification. Now shares code LOPEM2 with annual ryegrass.
Could_be_confused_with: Perennial ryegrass; Italian ryegrass; tall fescue; meadow fescue; festulolium

Why: Never recorded anywhere. Seed lot germinated at 26% and it is a wetland species, so failure is the expected result rather than an ID problem.

ID_reliability: Good in flower, poor as a rosette
Why: Flowering plants are unmistakable; vegetative rosettes are not, and several notes flag "is poss chicory??".
Reliable, but present in Control at 12 of 19 farms, so its presence in a seeded plot cannot be credited to the mix.
Distinctive pinnate leaves. Establishment is genuinely weak rather than an ID problem.
Notes at DS and TF read "smooth aster. dahlia-esque... maybe heliopsis? prob. Combine if yes", which is the same plant as the wingstem record.
Could_be_confused_with: WINGSTEM (Verbesina alternifolia); Maximilian sunflower; other yellow composites

Why: A DS note says "might have been calling this coneflower in past years" against lanceleaf coreopsis, so the two may be partly interchanged.
Same pair as above, in the other direction.
Never recorded. Seeded at 0.02 PLS/ft2 - the lowest density in the mix - so this is not a real test.
Distinctive when flowering. Seedlings are harder.
Tall and distinctive in flower. One mix note says senna was frost-seeded at some farms, which may complicate the record.
Never recorded anywhere. Distinctive pink raceme and pinnate leaves, so a genuine failure rather than a missed ID.
Never recorded. Distinctive. The seed-mix sheet notes it may have been lumped "as white clover", which is doubtful on morphology but worth checking against photos.
Could_be_confused_with: Nothing close; possibly recorded as generic clover

Why: Only trace records. Seeded at 0.02 PLS/ft2 from a 12%-germination lot, so not a real test. Volunteer annual lespedeza is abundant across the farms and could absorb records.
Could_be_confused_with: JAPANESE/COMMON LESPEDEZA (Kummerowia striata, abundant volunteer); sericea lespedeza

Why: Reliable - folded vernation and flattened sheath. But present in Control at 17 of 19 farms, so not attributable to the Low mix.
Merged into Schedonorus sp. at most plots during the fescue reclassification because it could not be separated from tall or meadow fescue. Only 3 farms retain a clean SCLO5 biomass record.
Could_be_confused_with: TALL FESCUE; meadow fescue; perennial ryegrass; hybrid ryegrass

Why: Only 1-2 farms retain a clean record; the rest sits inside the Schedonorus/Lolium complex.
Could_be_confused_with: Hybrid ryegrass; Italian ryegrass; tall and meadow fescue; festulolium

Why: Reliable as "red clover" but the mix also contained several other Trifolium species that were folded into red or white, so a red clover record is not proof the Ernst red clover established.
Could_be_confused_with: Other hairy-leaved Trifolium seeded in the High mix

Why: Same caveat, plus white clover is a near-universal resident (Control at 9 of 19 farms).
